kasasagicoffee.summary: Basement roastery cafe in Xinyi with a Showa-era feel, known for black sugar cream cold drip, tiramisu and dumplings with coffee sauces.
signature: Dumplings with coffee dipping sauces (咖啡醬料水餃)
Black sugar cream cold drip (黑糖奶油冰滴)
highlights: Signature cream cold drip is smooth and widely praised; tiramisu called generous
Dumplings come with three coffee-based sauces, a surprise hit
Staff patiently explain a wide range of beans; pet-friendly
lowlights: Time limit and a one-drink minimum per person
The basement echoes, so it can get loud
No reservations; last order at 17:00

kite_coffee_.summary: Tiny Da'an espresso bar run by a couple, a Sprudge 2023 Best New Cafe finalist, known for pudding, cheesecake and silky milk drinks.
signature: Salted egg red bean Basque cheesecake (鹹蛋紅豆泥巴斯克)
highlights: Pudding is repeatedly called a standout
Silky milk drinks with cute latte art, served in thin-walled cups
Good music and friendly owners; you can pay extra to switch beans
lowlights: Very small with few seats; better for a quick drink than a long stay
Chairs described as uncomfortable
Cheesecake a bit pricey; one found the SOE latte burnt and bitter

taiwan_rememberme_cafe.summary: Late-night cafe in a lane behind Nanjing East Road near Taipei Arena, open to 2am, with live singers, full meals and tiramisu.
signature: Mentaiko salmon pasta (明太子鮭魚義大利麵)
Crispy bacon cheese beef risotto (脆培起司牛肉燉飯)
highlights: Evening live singing gives the room a lively, intimate mood
Pasta, risotto and cakes rated well above typical cafe food
Open late, pet-friendly, quick and warm service; art books and doodles in the drawers
lowlights: Singers can be loud and the sound system harsh in the small room
Menus sit in table drawers, which staff do not always explain
3-hour limit when full; strong air-conditioning

coffeeunderwater.summary: Spacious blue-toned cafe on Longjiang Road near Nanjing Fuxing MRT, run by a 2024 Taiwan barista champion; known for tea coffees and cheesecake.
signature: Ripe mango tea latte (完熟芒果茶拿鐵)
highlights: Roomy seating; weekday walk-ins easy; good for work or study
Inventive tea-coffee blends plus many single origins; beans sold on site
Balanced pour-overs at fair prices
lowlights: Air-conditioning too strong; one report of curt staff over a seat change
Ice and sweetness can't be adjusted; one found the cappuccino weak
NT$130 minimum per person

yiyi.taipei.summary: Coffee-cocktail bar in Xinyi, reached via Lane 419, serving layered colour-themed drinks that mix coffee, tea and spirits.
highlights: Layered coffee cocktails served with tasting cards and explanations
Calm lighting and music; guests read over a drink
Friendly owners; non-alcoholic coffee-tea pairings too
lowlights: One visitor found the bar stools too low and the dim light hard on the tiny menu text
Same visitor felt staff ignored first-timers

whatslife.studio.summary: Dark, hushed roastery cafe in Datong near Xingtian Temple, pairing light-roast coffee with vinyl records and creative desserts.
highlights: Clean, floral light roasts and careful pour-overs
Inventive desserts such as pineapple salted-egg-yolk Basque
Quiet black interior, vinyl music and a resident cat
lowlights: Must speak softly; staff remind loud talkers, so not for chatting
Groups of up to four only, 2-hour limit when full, no bookings
Some desserts run on the sweet side

enroute_coffee.summary: Coffee-only roastery on Hulin Street near Yongchun MRT; no cakes, just single origins explained by staff plus sparkling coffee drinks.
highlights: Staff patiently explain each bean, brew method and flavour
Quiet, bright room with outlets; good for work or reading
Good value; ice balls keep iced drinks from diluting
lowlights: Small space
No desserts or snacks, only coffee

noon.taipei.summary: Unsigned concrete-walled cafe in a Rui'an Street lane in Da'an, known for its 1+1+1 coffee flight and shiso butter toast.
signature: Shiso butter toast (紫蘇抹醬奶油烤土司)
highlights: Skilled, consistent baristas; the flight ends in a sake or gin coffee cocktail
Calm wood-and-grey room with fresh flowers; pet-friendly
Toast and pastries pair well with the coffee
lowlights: 90-minute limit; walk-in only
Busy weekends: music a bit loud, staff rushed
Warm room melts ice fast; one found the espresso leg sour and plain

rufous_coffee_2.summary: Second branch of award-winning Rufous near Zhongshan Junior High MRT, known for floating cream cold drip and caramel cinnamon apple pie.
signature: Caramel cinnamon apple pie (焦糖肉桂蘋果派)
Floating cream cold drip (漂浮奶油冰滴)
Honey cinnamon cold drip (蜂蜜肉桂冰滴)
highlights: Warm, attentive staff help match coffee to your taste
Rich cold drip and well-extracted iced espresso drinks
Dim wood-and-retro room; guests keep voices low
lowlights: Often full; tables feel cramped
Busy at peak times

oasis_coffee_roasting_lab.summary: Minimalist Shilin roastery set back behind a courtyard of tall palms, from a Taiwan Brewers Cup champion team, focused on light-roast pour-overs.
signature: Washed Ethiopian espresso (水洗衣索比亞)
highlights: Staff explain each bean and its story with enthusiasm
Designed space with courtyard trees, chosen cups, outlets and Wi-Fi
Clean, balanced light roasts
lowlights: Crowded on weekends
Chairs are hard
Mostly light roasts; NT$160 Americano; milk coffee less distinctive

rokucyomecafe.summary: Homely Japanese-style cafe in a Minsheng Community lane, known for seasonal fruit chiffon cakes, pork curry rice and hojicha drinks.
signature: Japanese pork curry rice (日式豬肉咖哩飯)
Red wine beef stew (紅酒燉牛肉)
highlights: Fluffy, not-too-sweet chiffons with seasonal fruit
Mains such as curry and stews are solid, not afterthoughts
Warm, patient staff; cosy room; genuinely pet-friendly
lowlights: No reservations; weekend waits, with a call when your table is ready
3-hour limit when full
Some sweets on the sweet side; latte light on coffee

rufous_coffee_1.summary: Long-running Rufous flagship on Fuxing South Road near Technology Building MRT, known for cream cold drip, Geisha and apple pie.
signature: Caramel cinnamon apple pie (焦糖肉桂蘋果派)
highlights: Cold drip served over slow-melting ice; Geisha drip draws raves
Apple pie with ice cream is not too sweet
Friendly, professional staff; sunny window bar seats
lowlights: About 20-minute waits at busy times
Gets noisy when full
Cold drip and iced cappuccino too acidic for some

coffee_sind.summary: Tiny semi-outdoor coffee stand by Zhongxiao Xinsheng MRT Exit 5, No. 36 on 2026's World's 100 Best list, known for its torched-sugar latte.
signature: Nantou Hua Yin estate pour-over (南投花音莊園)
highlights: Cheerful owner and staff suggest beans by taste and bring water
Sugar latte with crackly torched top, like a liquid crème brûlée
Succulents and air plants decorate the stand
lowlights: Few seats, mostly outdoors; hot in summer
Pour-overs can take 20-30 minutes
Plain storefront; opens to non-regulars at 2pm

kingmauiitp02.summary: Two-storey, pet-friendly all-day brunch cafe in Luzhou, known for hearty brunch plates, truffle dishes and cold drip coffee.
signature: Truffle mushroom omelette (松露野菇歐姆蛋)
Sous-vide chicken omelette brunch (舒肥雞胸歐姆蛋早午餐)
highlights: Generous, well-seasoned brunch plates
Bright, clean, roomy space suited to groups and pets
Friendly service; parking nearby
lowlights: Prices slightly high

kikumo.taipei.summary: Tiny takeaway-focused espresso bar in Zhongshan with big windows, known for flat whites, dirties and pork floss Basque cheesecake.
signature: Pork floss Basque cheesecake (肉鬆巴斯克)
Pistachio Basque cheesecake (開心果巴斯克)
highlights: Rich lattes and a Melbourne-style flat white
Molten Basque cheesecakes, especially pork floss
Friendly owner, good music, phone charging
lowlights: Few seats at an awkward height; no toilet
Solo barista means about 10-minute waits
Smokers sometimes on the outside bench

branchroasters.summary: Small coffee-only roastery on Ren'ai Road, about 7 minutes from Zhongxiao Dunhua MRT, known for carbonated espresso and Geisha pour-overs.
signature: Peru Los Santos Geisha (秘魯桑托斯藝伎)
highlights: Friendly, knowledgeable baristas explain beans in detail
Inventive formats like CO2 espresso and frozen-milk Double Crush
Calm wood room, no time limit, Wi-Fi and outlets
lowlights: Few seats, around 18
Coffee only, no other drinks

beamcoast.coffee.summary: Dark-wood, Japanese-style corner coffee bar in an East District lane near Zhongxiao Dunhua MRT, known for honey cinnamon and lemon coffees.
signature: Honey cinnamon latte (蜂蜜肉桂拿鐵)
highlights: Smooth, fragrant coffee in small, easy-drinking cups
Stylish wood design and distinctive cups
Expanded seating and no time limit
lowlights: Seats fill up on weekends, forcing takeaway
Small; not suited to laptops or groups
Hojicha milk mild

neighborhood_coffee_tw_2022.summary: Garden cafe and roastery in an old house off Zhongzheng Road, Xinzhuang, near Huilong MRT, known for boozy tiramisu and Basque cheesecake.
signature: Taro pork floss croissant (芋泥肉鬆可頌)
Sea salt pineapple Americano (海鹽鳳梨美式)
highlights: Moist tiramisu with gentle liqueur, reordered by regulars
Creative croissants and cakes; good lattes
Leafy old-house setting, quiet music, pet-friendly
lowlights: Lane parking is hard; paid lot nearby
Taro croissant seen as overpriced by one
Osmanthus latte overpowering; chiffon weaker than others

nowchance_fuxing.summary: Small wood-toned coffee and dessert bar from Now Chance roasters on Zhongshan's Fuxing side, known for fruit coffees and tea pudding.
signature: Earl Grey tea pudding (伯爵茶罐布丁)
Pomelo jin xuan roll cake (柚香金萱生乳捲)
Smoked green apple beef focaccia (煙燻青蘋果牛肉起司佛卡夏)
highlights: Desserts and sandwiches beat expectations
Distinctive fruit coffees and good pour-overs
Friendly owner; water for those waiting outside
lowlights: Only about three tables; waitlist at peak
90-minute limit
Pudding sits in too much syrup; honey cinnamon latte watery for some

saturn_landing_turkish_coffee.summary: Turkish coffee house that moved from Yongkang Street to near Taipei City Hall, serving spiced coffee, künefe, rice pudding and tarot.
signature: Cumin lamb stuffed bread (孜然羊肉手工麵包)
highlights: Authentic Turkish desserts, less sweet than in the Middle East
Hearty mains and breads made to order
Cosy, quiet room with tarot and coffee-ground readings
lowlights: Prices on the high side
Spiced Turkish coffee is divisive
Service uneven; menu options not always explained

vwibychadwang.summary: Chad Wang's light-roast specialty cafe, moved from the Breeze area to a park-corner East District lane, known for pour-overs and tiramisu.
highlights: Precise light-roast pour-overs from a World Brewers Cup champion
Quiet park-corner setting; staff speak good English
Desserts like apple mille-feuille praised
lowlights: Often full; waits for a table
Limited ground-floor seating, some without tables
Some find the coffee acidic or the food ordinary

jellyjellytaipei.summary: Korean-style cake cafe on Linyi Street in Zhongzheng, known for pandan and jasmine milk green cakes plus tofu noodles and curry.
signature: Jasmine milk green cake (茉莉花奶綠蛋糕)
Black sesame cake (黑金芝麻蛋糕)
Peach Earl Grey cake (蜜桃伯爵茶蛋糕)
Sicilian lemon coffee (西西里檸檬咖啡)
highlights: Light, not-too-sweet layered cakes with mousse and jelly
Thoughtful savoury meals such as tofu noodles and stews
Friendly staff; reservations accepted
lowlights: Few seats; crowded at the order counter
Coffee average, small lattes
Sauce portions small for the rice; 2-hour limit on weekends

2730.cafe.summary: Retro old-house cafe with resident cats in a Da'an lane by Xinyi; known for Basque cheesecakes and homestyle rice plates.
signature: Grandma's braised pork rice (阿嬤的控肉飯)
highlights: Friendly cats, especially the white one, plus vintage goods and a consignment corner
Quiet, relaxed room with roomy tables and bookshelves; no time limit on weekdays
Homestyle food; the dumplings stay crisp and the Basque cakes are well balanced
lowlights: Drunken chicken rice criticised: hard rice, chicken that tasted long refrigerated
Some dishes run salty or sweet: dry curry, bittersweet chocolate milk
No reservations, whole party must be present to sit, 3-hour limit on weekends

mitsuocoffee.summary: Bright corner coffee bar in a Taiyuan Road lane near Taipei Main Station, known for pudding with white miso ice cream.
signature: Pudding with white miso ice cream (布丁搭白味噌冰淇淋)
highlights: House-roasted pour-overs with bright citrus and berry notes, explained at the table
Firm caramel pudding with salty-sweet miso ice cream
Old house with glass walls, plenty of light, and friendly staff
lowlights: Prices on the high side
90-minute limit when full; closes at 17:00 and on Tuesdays

jiaojiao_cafe.summary: Tiny, very quiet dessert cafe near Jingmei Night Market in Wenshan, known for chiffon cakes with tea-flavoured creams.
signature: Tieguanyin walnut caramel crunch chiffon (鐵觀音核桃焦糖脆脆戚風)
Caramel nut chiffon (焦糖核果戚風)
Rum raisin Basque (萊姆葡萄巴斯克)
Jiao sugar crunch milk tea (嬌糖脆脆)
highlights: Fluffy, moist chiffon with light, not-too-sweet cream
Custom cakes ordered via LINE, made with care for special requests
Neat latte art, clean room, no service charge
lowlights: Strict hush rule; not for chatting, and small noises feel stressful
Few seats, self-service, cash only, 2-hour limit, no groups over four
Staff come across cold to some

alchemist.tw.summary: Singapore specialty coffee brand's Dihua branch on a Nanjing West Road lane: a small minimalist bar with two espresso blends and pour-overs.
highlights: Two espresso blends to choose from for milk drinks
Friendly, attentive baristas
Calm, minimalist design; a quiet stop while walking Dadaocheng
lowlights: Very few seats, all facing the counter
English-only, short menu
Ring a button to enter; smaller than expected

after5_coffeetail.summary: Two-storey wooden loft cafe on a Linsen North Road lane by Zhong'an Park, known for cinnamon rolls and clean espresso.
signature: Masala chai latte (瑪薩拉茶拿鐵)
highlights: Clean, bright medium-roast espresso and Taiwanese single origins
Friendly owner and staff who explain the coffee menu
Renovated old house; upstairs back seats feel like a private nook
lowlights: Small and crowded; some suggest taking out to the park
Table and chair heights don't match
One reviewer found it ordinary next to other cafes

ogawa.coffee.summary: Garden coffee stand on a Wuxing Street corner near Taipei 101, known for fruity pour-overs and guava coffee outdoors.
signature: Red guava coffee (紅心芭樂咖啡)
highlights: Leafy back-garden seating with gravel and woven blinds, a calm break in Xinyi
Around 20 pour-over beans; light roasts with clear fruit notes
Friendly owners; dog-friendly
lowlights: Only about 10 outdoor seats; hot at summer noon with just fans
Paper cups only; americano a bit thin

coffee_dumbo.summary: Tiny retro cafe on Chifeng Street in Datong, known for warm American-style cinnamon rolls and an 80s vintage look.
highlights: Cinnamon rolls warmed to order: soft, moist, fragrant, not too sweet
Vintage decor, playful cups, and a clinic chair out front draw photos
Attentive, friendly staff; pudding with a strong egg flavour
lowlights: No restroom
Very few seats, 1-hour limit, no groups over four; takeout recommended
Waits likely; arrive early

sidoli_radio.summary: Retro cassette-themed cafe and record store about 5 minutes from Beimen MRT, with a basement of tapes and vinyl.
signature: Brown sugar cream cold brew (黑糖奶油冷萃)
Earl Grey milk tea (伯爵奶茶)
highlights: Designed by Fang Xu-zhong; dim retro room around a skylight
Basement of cassettes and vinyl; tape players to borrow; weekend DJs
Outlets at every seat and a spotless restroom
lowlights: Under 10 small tables; cramped and often a wait
2-hour limit enforced even when not full
Some complain about staff attitude

ooparts_kissa.summary: Japanese-style kissaten on a Chengde Road lane in Datong, known for Napolitan spaghetti, pudding and no time limit.
highlights: Wood, velvet sofas and two walls of windows onto greenery
No time limit, outlets, and plenty of books; good for reading or work
Friendly owner; coffee and food both solid
lowlights: Fills at opening; waits of 30+ minutes
Pasta sauce reads sour or sweet to some
Prices on the refined side

twinbrotherscoffee.summary: Roaster cafe on Huayin Street beside Taipei Main Station, known for its handmade cinnamon rolls and good-value coffee.
signature: Walnut bittersweet chocolate pie (核桃苦甜巧克力派)
Basque burnt cheesecake (巴斯克焦香乳酪蛋糕)
highlights: Moist, fragrant cinnamon rolls that aren't overly sweet; reheat well
Low prices for drinks and pastries; crisp-crust canelés and tarts
Friendly staff, kid-friendly, open from 7:30 for breakfast
lowlights: Cinnamon rolls not out until about 11am
90-minute limit, cash only, mostly two-person tables
Coffee described as middling; soft rolls lack chew for some

coffeeimmerse.summary: Small specialty cafe about 6 minutes from Liuzhangli MRT, known for smooth lattes and fruity light-roast espresso.
highlights: Smooth milk drinks with fruity Ethiopian-led espresso; pour-overs praised too
Owners are warm and explain each coffee
Clean, comfortable, pet-friendly, with outdoor seats
lowlights: Often full even on weekdays; about 16 seats, 1.5-hour limit when busy
Espresso drinks run strong for light caffeine drinkers

moonshine_coffee.summary: Industrial-style roaster flagship on Dunhua South Road, Da'an, known for customisable espresso and a boozy tiramisu.
highlights: Choose roast, bean, decaf and shot count; clear menu
Grown-up tiramisu with a strong liqueur note
Friendly staff; sleek neon-lit space suited to working
lowlights: Some find the coffee weak or ordinary
Small cup sizes, noted on delivery orders

kaffe_24.summary: Nordic-style roaster in a standalone old house off Xinyi Road near Zhongxiao Fuxing, known for apple pie and pour-overs.
highlights: Leafy old house with terrazzo stairs and upstairs window seats
Owner recommends pour-overs to suit the day; floral, fruity light roasts
Calm, quiet room good for reading
lowlights: Drinks run NT$180–800 a cup or pot
Hushed atmosphere; not a place for lively group chats

ironwood.coffee.summary: Second-floor cafe up a hidden stair near Zhongshan MRT, known for cream-heavy chiffon cakes and its rum-almond latte.
signature: Red velvet strawberry cream cake (紅絲絨草莓奶油蛋糕)
Fig cream cocoa chiffon (無花果奶油可可戚風)
Strawberry cream cake (草莓鮮奶蛋糕)
Cherry chocolate cream cake (櫻桃巧克力奶油蛋糕)
highlights: Smooth, milky cream that isn't too sweet; moist cake
House drink Ironwood blends almond and rum into a latte
Vintage wood room; photogenic
lowlights: Waits of 40 minutes to over an hour on weekends; register to queue
Lots of cream; cakes get rich and filling strawberries sparse
Drinks average: thin americano, bitter matcha, few tea options

rihfengco.summary: Dessert cafe inside a working car repair shop in Xinzhuang, known for black sesame chiffon and cream-topped americano.
signature: Kuki black sesame chiffon (九鬼黑芝麻戚風)
Honey citron black tea (蜂蜜柚子紅茶)
highlights: Soft, moist chiffon with rich sesame paste and light cream
Quirky garage setting: jacks, motor oil, an engine as decor
Smooth coffee at low prices; owners polite and relaxed
lowlights: Few seats; 1-hour limit when people are waiting
Small drink cups; no Wi-Fi

olocoffeeroasters.summary: Library-quiet roaster cafe in the Zhongshan area, known for egg salad sandwiches, pound cake and reading in silence.
signature: Cheese egg salad sandwich (起司蛋沙拉三明治)
Cheese pork cutlet egg salad sandwich (起司豬排蛋沙拉三明治)
highlights: Near-silent room with books and manga, ideal for reading or focused work
Fine, creamy egg salad sandwiches; banana pound cake strongly praised
Well-chosen music; owner shy but friendly
lowlights: Silence feels tense; some worry about noise even while eating
Occasional curt staff, especially when busy
Cash only, 3-hour limit for non-regulars, not cheap for the portions

wenshanroasting1983.summary: Retro, dimly lit roaster cafe near Jingmei Night Market, known for single-origin pour-overs and lemon glazed pound cake.
signature: Lemon glazed pound cake (檸檬糖霜磅蛋糕)
highlights: Wood-heavy interior evoking an old Japanese-era coffee house
Distinctive single origins, with staff explaining the differences
Wide range of beans to buy; window seats face a park
lowlights: Latte at NT$200 seen as pricey
One phone takeaway order came out wrong

bosancafe.summary: Dim Japanese-style coffee bar in Zhongshan playing vinyl jazz on vintage hi-fi, known for kumquat coffee and cold drip.
highlights: Darker, Japanese-style roasts; flavourful single-origin pour-overs
Jazz records on vintage Altec and McIntosh gear; quirky collectibles
Owner works solo yet refills water; no limit when not full
lowlights: Owner's brusque manner puts some off
Tiny desserts that feel pricey; few dessert choices
Groups capped at three; food smells like curry drift in

olivia_coffee_roaster.summary: Small roaster in an east Da'an lane, known for its foamy lemon iced americano and 2020 Taiwan creative coffee title.
signature: Lemon foam iced americano (雷夢冰美式)
highlights: Dense foam and lemon make a refreshing, beer-like summer drink
Balanced cappuccino and latte; knowledgeable staff
Clean little room and a friendly Pomeranian shop dog
lowlights: Half-foam drinks feel empty to some
Pour-over thin, cheesecake dry at times
High stools make it less suited to lounging

now__chance.summary: Wood-toned roaster cafe on a Yonghe ground floor, known for picking your own bean and brew plus small creative desserts.
signature: Canelé trio in a steamer (可麗露)
Chestnut cream black tea chiffon (栗子奶油紅茶戚風)
Roasted oolong Basque (焙茶烏龍巴斯克)
highlights: Wide single-origin choice; pick the bean, then the brew method
Creative desserts, with canelés served in a little bamboo steamer
Calm Japanese-style wood room; friendly staff; pet-friendly
lowlights: Very small portions; food and drink often over NT$300
Crowded shared table, few outlets, no bag baskets
Seating order handled poorly; pudding sells out

oasis_coffee_roasters_anhe.summary: Compact roaster bar on Anhe Road in Da'an, run by award-winning brewers, known for cold drip, flat whites and cinnamon rolls.
highlights: Clean, well-made coffee from a brewing-competition team
Staff patiently guide bean and oat-milk choices
Friendly service; the cinnamon roll is recommended
lowlights: About 20 seats; weekend waits around 30 minutes
Noisy, with uncomfortable seats; not for lingering
Seating rules applied unevenly; few non-coffee options

goodman_roaster_taipei.summary: Japanese-run roaster in a quiet Tianmu residential lane in Shilin, known for Alishan pour-overs, lattes and pound cake.
highlights: Distinctive pour-overs, like the light, peachy, tea-like Alishan
Calm indoor and semi-outdoor seats; no set time limit
Owner-roaster Sato's beans widely praised; staff friendly
lowlights: Small cups for the price; cash only
Hard to reach, with scarce parking
One report of a 20-minute wait while bean buyers were served first

luguocafe.summary: House-roasting café a minute from Guandu MRT Exit 1, open since 2006; known for its shop cats, cold drip and banana pound cake.
signature: Banana chocolate pound cake (香蕉巧克力磅蛋糕)
Iced caramel macchiato (冰焦糖瑪奇朵)
highlights: The shop cats are the main draw for many visitors
Well-roasted beans; daily pour-overs with a light option and a rich one
Relaxed neighbourhood feel, clean space, roomy restroom, friendly owner
lowlights: Few seats and a somewhat cramped room
One cat, Biru, is a former stray that may bite, so approach gently

oasis_coffee_roasters_nanjing.summary: Small light-roast café near Nanjing Fuxing MRT, the third Oasis branch; known for lattes, cold drip and rotating pour-overs.
highlights: Baristas explain the day's beans and let you smell them before ordering
Balanced espresso-and-milk drinks; bright, layered light-roast pour-overs
Sunlit concrete-toned room with carefully chosen glassware
lowlights: Micro-sized shop, more a pit stop than a place to linger
Only a few single-origin options on a given day

hobo_place.summary: Dim, retro old-house café in Zhongshan with groups capped at three; known for caramel pudding, egg salad toast and tiramisu.
signature: Egg salad thick toast (蛋沙拉烤厚片)
Kinako brown sugar latte (黃豆粉黑糖拿鐵)
highlights: Firm, grown-up pudding with bitter, barely sweet caramel
Crisp thick toast loaded with well-spiced egg salad
Quiet nostalgic interior; staff friendlier than the strict signs suggest
lowlights: No bookings, max three per group, no splitting tables
Time limit: three hours on weekdays, two on weekends
Often full; you sign up at the closed door and are asked not to wait outside

p.coffee_roaster.summary: Tiny roaster-café and florist about 8 minutes from Jingmei MRT, with a cosy upstairs room; known for Americano and lemon Sicilian.
signature: Baked cinnamon apple pastry (烤肉桂蘋果巧酥)
highlights: Medium-roast espresso blend plus light-roast single origins; well balanced
Cosy, thoughtfully decorated second floor that stays quiet
Warm, friendly owners; beans sold in many varieties and sizes
lowlights: Upstairs seating is narrow, about 10 seats, not for long stays
Two-hour limit on weekends and a one-drink minimum

cafexiaomijo.summary: Library-quiet café about 7 minutes from Linguang MRT where guests whisper; known for carrot cake, egg salad sandwiches and chiffon.
signature: Egg salad sandwich (蛋沙拉三明治)
Pineapple shrimp ciabatta (鳳梨鮮蝦拖鞋麵包)
highlights: Enforced quiet, no time limit, Wi-Fi and sockets: ideal for study and work
Moist carrot cake with lemon cream; savoury dishes also impress
Friendly owners; daily desserts posted on Instagram stories
lowlights: Not for chatting; loud guests get a reminder, outdoor seats for talkers
Cash only and fills up on weekends
Some drinks small for the price; occasional last-minute closures

simplekaffa.summary: Spacious Huashan flagship of the 2016 World Barista Champion's café in Zhongzheng; known for pour-overs, honey cake and tiramisu.
signature: Half-baked honey cake (皺皺半熟蜂蜜蛋糕)
highlights: Layered, award-level coffee, including the champion's batch pour-over
Large, characterful space; attentive, focused staff
Creative drinks and desserts such as the four-liquor tiramisu
lowlights: Queues even on weekdays; 90-minute limit when people are waiting
Some find the coffee good but not memorable given the fame
Daytime hours only; parking nearby is difficult

instilcoffee.summary: Minimalist specialty café near Zhongshan MRT Exit 6, off Chengde Road; known for barista-guided pour-overs and cream roll cakes.
signature: Sea salt caramel roll cake (海鹽焦糖蛋糕卷)
highlights: Staff explain each day's beans in detail before you order
Pour-overs evolve as they cool; signature drinks surprise
Calm, dark-toned minimalist interior just off busy Zhongshan
lowlights: Pricey: a small latte runs NT$210
Some find the coffee on the acidic side
Two-hour limit, no cards (LINE Pay accepted), no bookings

southcity_coffee.summary: Small pour-over specialist near Zhongxiao East Road and Keelung Road in Xinyi; known for single origins, Basque cake and chiffon.
signature: Tieguanyin Basque cheesecake (鐵觀音巴斯克)
highlights: Owner explains each pour-over; cards list origin, altitude and flavour
Desserts and pasta well above typical café standard
Calm, refined little room; thoughtful touches in the restroom
lowlights: Pour-overs can take a while
Tight space; cash, bank transfer or Taiwan Pay only
One visitor found the cream cold brew watery and a staff remark rude

candocoffeetw.summary: House-roasting café near Longshan Temple MRT in Wanhua with plenty of seats; known for quiche, cinnamon rolls and pasta.
highlights: Wide menu: quiches, cinnamon rolls, pasta, cakes and decaf options
Friendly staff who explain the coffees; clean restrooms
Many seats, wall sockets and Wi-Fi
lowlights: Gets noisy when busy
Two-hour limit; no credit cards
Lattes in glass cool quickly; some drinks only average

fikafikacafe.summary: Large, bright café beside Yitong Park near Songjiang Nanjing MRT; known for upbeat staff, cinnamon rolls and light and dark roasts.
signature: Tieguanyin half-and-half latte (半半鐵觀音拿鐵)
highlights: Energetic, friendly staff are the most praised feature
Coffee widely liked, with light and dark roast choices
Roomy space with indoor and outdoor seats and plenty of sockets
lowlights: Full of laptop users; seats hard to find later in the day
Food uneven: quiche called hollow, tiramisu soggy, chicken dry
Cinnamon roll too sweet for some; fruit flies reported

quartet.kaffe.summary: Quiet light-roast pour-over bar on Hongguo Road in Banqiao; known for clean, aromatic pour-overs and a bittersweet caramel pudding.
highlights: Clean, aromatic pour-overs brewed at two temperatures, served in wide cups
Firm bittersweet caramel pudding pairs well with the coffee
Calm Japanese-style room with classical music; the owner's taste shows
lowlights: Few seats; not suited to groups or laptop work
Short hours: open Thursday to Sunday afternoons only

joeunnalcafe.summary: Korean-named café in the Minsheng Community, about 10 minutes from Nanjing Sanmin MRT; known for corn latte, tiramisu and egg salad.
signature: Egg salad sandwich (蛋沙拉三明治)
Black sugar cappuccino (黑糖卡布奇諾)
highlights: Inventive drinks: corn latte with fine foam, black sugar cappuccino, coffee cocktails
No time limit, sockets and Wi-Fi; suits work or catching up
Simple, calm space with outdoor tables and very friendly staff
lowlights: Often nearly full by mid-afternoon
Cold drip au lait leans bitter for some

ferment_banqiao.summary: Moroccan-styled café in a Banqiao lane near a market, 8 minutes from Fuzhong MRT; known for croissant sandwiches and tiramisu.
signature: Brie and bolognese croissant sandwich (布里起司義式肉醬可頌三明治)
Lemon avocado sourdough sandwich (輕檸酪梨酸種三明治)
Charlotte fruity latte (夏綠蒂果香拿鐵)
Osmanthus ginger milk tea (桂花薑汁鮮奶茶)
highlights: Crisp brie and bolognese croissant sandwich is the standout
Thoughtful design, good light, plenty of seats and sockets
Friendly service; quieter before 2pm
lowlights: Sourdough crusts on the sandwiches are hard
Pricey for the portions; small chairs and tables
Restroom is upstairs and shared; pasta served only until 13:30

single_origin_espresso_roast.summary: Light-roast roaster's tasting room above a barbershop on Wuxing Street, opposite TMU Hospital; known for pour-overs and 1+1 sets.
highlights: Owner Ah Ji brews expertly; bar seats let you watch up close
Wide choice of light-roast beans and brew methods
Bright room with four large glass walls; relaxed and friendly
lowlights: Opens only a few days a month, so check Instagram first
Tiny, roughly six seats, and the entrance is easy to miss
Desserts not always available

kooncoffee0801.summary: Small light-roast roaster with a blue-and-white storefront on the edge of Sanchong; known for fruity lattes, flat whites and drip bags.
highlights: Fruity light-roast milk drinks win over even acidity sceptics
Pour-overs change nicely from hot to cool
Silky tiramisu; consistent beans and drip bags to take home
lowlights: Cramped seating makes it hard to fully relax
Pricey for takeaway coffee
Owner is reserved and blunt, which not everyone warms to

ninedayscoffee.summary: Compact, takeaway-focused roaster bar near Taipei Main Station and NTU Hospital; known for rich lattes and warm staff.
highlights: Lattes are the headline: rich, smooth and specialty-grade
Warm, enthusiastic staff
Light-roast pour-overs and English milk tea also praised
lowlights: Tiny seating area
Some find it less aromatic than the Fuxing branch
One report of an inattentive cashier on her phone

mingscoffeeplayroom.summary: Pet-friendly house-roasting café on a Tamsui slope with plenty of sockets and no time limit; known for lattes and cheesecakes.
highlights: Rich, smooth lattes and pour-overs from the owner's own roasts
Spacious and quiet, many sockets, no time limit: good for work
Friendly owner; homemade desserts, flexible minimum and a loyalty card
lowlights: Limited food, mostly a few desserts
Best reached by scooter or on foot; parking is hard on the slope

daonanguan_specialty_coffee.summary: Taipei outpost of a veteran Tainan light-roast roaster, in an Anhe Road lane in Da'an; known for hand-brewed single origins.
highlights: Owner's roasting is widely respected; some have followed it for 10+ years
Owner chats readily about coffee and vinyl records
Minimal Japanese-style room centred on a big wooden bar
lowlights: Small room that can feel a little stuffy

aromacafetaipei.summary: Seventh-floor café on Guanqian Road near Taipei Main Station; known for English conversation nights, no time limit and pizza.
signature: Bacon cream pasta (培根奶油義大利麵)
highlights: Warm staff and owner, several fluent in English
Roomy second floor with sofas, Wi-Fi and sockets; no time limit
Thursday and Friday evening English conversation sessions
lowlights: Cash only, no e-payments
Not cheap for the area, with a latte near Starbucks prices
Some dishes oily; fruit tea light on tea flavour

gazecafe.summary: House-roasting café that doubles as an eyewear shop, near Longshan Temple in Wanhua; known for cinnamon rolls and lemon tart.
signature: New York cheesecake (紐約起司蛋糕)
highlights: Many pour-over choices from award-winning in-house roasts
Friendly staff; bright, clean room with Wi-Fi and sockets
Reasonable prices; cinnamon rolls and cakes well liked
lowlights: Few seats and the high stools are uncomfortable
Drinks can take a while to arrive

congratscafe.summary: Two-storey old-house roaster café on Wenchang Street, 3 minutes from Xinyi Anhe MRT; known for cinnamon rolls and guava Americano.
signature: Black tea chiffon cake (紅茶戚風蛋糕)
Pistachio rare cheesecake (開心果生乳酪)
highlights: Owner matches pour-over beans to your taste; inventive guava Americano
Airy high-ceilinged upstairs with sockets; open until 8pm
Silky cream cold drip and pistachio cheesecake draw praise
lowlights: Smoking area out front; some notice smoke drifting in
Cinnamon roll and some milk drinks called bland or underwhelming
Busy, dusty upstairs, and a 2.5-hour limit on weekends
